scope.current_boundary: Teach linear momentum as the product of mass and velocity (p = mv), vector nature, sign conventions in 1D, and force as rate of change of momentum (F = Delta p / Delta t = ma for constant mass, F = v Delta m / Delta t for varying mass), including impulse and force-time / momentum-time graphs. Do not pre-teach Newton's first or third laws, weight W = mg, friction, drag, terminal velocity, conservation of linear momentum, or collisions.
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l01: mass as inertia, resultant force as vector sum, F = ma for constant mass, acceleration and net force always sharing the same direction.
Assumes kinematics concepts from Topic 2: displacement, velocity, acceleration as rate of change of velocity, sign conventions in one dimension.

immediate_previous.boundary: Mass is the property of an object that resists change in motion (inertia) and F = ma for constant mass.
can_assume: mass as property of a body resisting changes in motion
resultant force as vector sum of all forces
acceleration always in the same direction as resultant force

immediate_next.boundary: Newton's laws of motion: formal statement and application of first, second, and third laws; weight as gravitational force W = mg.
must_not_preteach: formal statement of Newton's first law and third law
principle of conservation of momentum (Topic 3 module 3)

calculation_checks.independent_working: Delta V / Delta t = A * v = 4.0e-4 m^2 * 35 m s^-1 = 0.014 m^3 s^-1. Delta m / Delta t = rho * (Delta V / Delta t) = 1000 kg m^-3 * 0.014 m^3 s^-1 = 14 kg s^-1.
